svg.text: 1. Most systems use single-leader for the primary write path.
LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter, Gmail, WhatsApp — all single-leader-per-shard.
2. Multi-leader ONLY when concurrent edits to the same mutable object are the product.
3. Strong global consistency (Spanner/Paxos) ONLY when correctness > latency.
Payments, permissions, ad billing, inventory. NOT social feeds or play counts.
4. Read paths are always more sophisticated than write paths.
Writes: "put it in source of truth." Reads: precomputed timelines, caches, search indexes, ML ranking.
5. No single database does everything. Polyglot persistence + event streams.
Espresso → Kafka → Venice / Galene / Pinot / Liquid. CQRS: normalized writes, denormalized reads.
